analysis.title: DeskTalk - Update on the US consumer: Retail therapy
key_insights: Walmart's earnings, together with October retail sales, reinforce US consumer resilience and give a constructive signal going into the holiday season.
Citi's consumer specialist salesperson described Walmart's guidance as 'dead inline'.
Walmart sits in the 'investor apathy' bucket of Citi's crowding monitor and trades at valuations above 40x, so the print is unlikely to bring sidelined investors back in.

Walmart's share gains in the latest quarter were led by shoppers with annual incomes over $100,000, a group not historically associated with the chain. This suggests wealthier households are becoming more selective.
Walmart management said shoppers are feeling some pressure from higher fuel prices, but spending remains reasonably strong.

The note says the Walmart data adds nuance to last week's K-shaped economy view. Higher-income households are becoming more value conscious, while lower-income consumers remain exposed to higher fuel, transportation and essential costs.

Walmart's CFO said shoppers stocked up on propane, bottled water and camping gear during this month's cyber scares. This 'preparedness shopping' has abated somewhat, and it tends to pull demand forward.
Citi concludes that consumer staples appear well placed heading into the holiday season.
Citi credit card data improved as of last week, but Citi economists still see spending risks tilted to the downside over the medium term.
Restaurant prices rose 0.5% MoM in October CPI, unexpectedly strong, which suggests real restaurant spending could fall in October.
